Bottleneck Distance Between Persistence Diagrams

Source: R/ph_distances.R
bottleneck_distance.Rd

bottleneck_distance() returns the bottleneck distance between two persistence diagrams, one value per homology dimension. It takes two persistent_homology() results, or two data frames of persistence pairs. For the finite pairs, the distance is $$W_\infty(D_1, D_2) = \inf_{\gamma} \sup_{p \in D_1} \|p - \gamma(p)\|_\infty,$$ where \(\gamma\) ranges over bijections \(D_1 \cup \Delta \to D_2 \cup \Delta\) and \(\Delta = \{(x,x)\}\) is the diagonal. Each point is matched to a point of the other diagram or to its projection onto the diagonal, at cost \(|d - b|/2\).

The distance is the largest shift needed to match the two diagrams' features: a small value means every feature of either diagram has a close counterpart in the other or is short-lived enough to sit near the diagonal. It is a distance between two observed diagrams and carries no sampling uncertainty of its own; to compare diagrams on a common grid, or to average several, use persistence_landscape().

Usage

bottleneck_distance(d1, d2, dimension = NULL, tol = .Machine$double.eps^0.5)

Arguments

d1, d2

The two diagrams: persistent_homology() results, or data frames with the columns dimension, birth and death (other columns are ignored). Any other input, or a data frame missing one of those columns, raises an error.

dimension

The homology dimensions to compare, as whole numbers. Default NULL: every dimension that appears in either diagram. A dimension absent from both gives 0.

tol

The tolerance added to each candidate cost when checking whether a matching exists, so that floating-point error does not miss an exact match. Default .Machine$double.eps ^ 0.5.

Value

A named numeric vector with one distance per dimension, named "dim_<k>" (empty when there is no dimension to compare). Inf marks a structural mismatch: different numbers of essential classes in that dimension. The distance of a diagram to itself is 0.

Details

The smallest feasible \(\varepsilon\) is found by binary search over the candidate costs (every pairwise \(L_\infty\) distance and every diagonal projection), checking each with a Kuhn bipartite matching.

Essential classes (death = Inf in VR mode, death = 0 with birth > 0 in clique mode, as persistence_landscape() reads them; a (0, 0) pair is a zero-length finite point) are matched one-to-one within each dimension by their sorted births. When the two diagrams have different numbers of essential classes in a dimension, the distance for that dimension is Inf.

References

Edelsbrunner, H. & Harer, J. (2010). Computational Topology: An Introduction. AMS. Section VIII.

Examples

mat1 <- matrix(c(0, .6, .5, .6, 0, .4, .5, .4, 0), 3, 3)
rownames(mat1) <- colnames(mat1) <- c("A","B","C")
ph1 <- persistent_homology(mat1, n_steps = 5)
bottleneck_distance(ph1, ph1)  # self-distance is 0
#> dim_0 
#>     0
